body:
## Status

**Adopted 0.3.0 type-theory synthesis.**

This issue records the conceptual core of the Qleisli 0.3.0 type system. Concrete boundary conveniences, canonical coercions, pattern richness and elaboration policy are deferred to **#197 (0.4.0 boundary conditions)**.

Related:
- #22 — ordinary data is unmarked; remove `CBit/CBits`
- #43 — `Unit` / `Q<Unit>`
- #84 — definitional equality / coherence / physical maps
- #89 — callable model
- #194 — `qfor`
- #195 — `qmatch`
- #196 — `q*** / Q<T> / unmarked` surface boundary
- #197 — 0.4.0 boundary-condition umbrella

## Adopted conceptual core

### 1. One ordinary finite type universe

Conceptually:

```text
T ::= Unit | Bit | Bits<n> | T × T | finite ordinary ADTs | ...
```

These are ordinary values.

There is no parallel source-level classical modality:

```text
C<T>      // not part of the adopted model
CBit      // removed in 0.3.0
CBits<n>  // removed in 0.3.0
```

The ordinary world is the baseline.

### 2. Quantum ownership is one explicit type constructor

Conceptually:

```text
Q<T>
```

means **linear quantum ownership over the finite basis/value space `T`**.

Examples:

```text
Bit          ordinary bit
Q<Bit>       quantum-owned bit basis

Bits<n>      ordinary finite bit sequence
Q<Bits<n>>   quantum-owned register

Unit         ordinary singleton
Q<Unit>      one-dimensional quantum ownership; scalar phase still matters
```

This gives the central type-level law:

> **Classical is not a modality in Qleisli. Quantum is.**

### 3. Ownership and effects are orthogonal

Typing judgments are organized conceptually as:

```text
Γ ; Δ ⊢ e : T ! ε
```

where:

- `Γ` contains unrestricted ordinary/static values;
- `Δ` contains linear quantum owners;
- `ε` is the declared/computed semantic effect.

The exact public effect spelling is tracked separately, but the structural separation is fixed:

- `Q<T>` is an ownership distinction, not an effect;
- quantum owners cannot be copied or implicitly discarded;
- ordinary values are unrestricted where their type permits;
- effects compose independently of ownership.

### 4. Three-level surface boundary

The type system aligns with #196:

```text
q***      construct itself has quantum semantics
Q<T>      ordinary syntax over quantum-owned data
unmarked  ordinary classical/static syntax
```

Canonical examples:

```text
if      / qif
for     / qfor
match   / qmatch
```

A `q` prefix is not decoration. It appears only when the construct itself changes semantics.

### 5. Static operation descriptions remain distinct from live owners

Keep the conceptual separation:

```text
Q<T>      live linear quantum ownership
Op<...>   static/program description
```

Higher-order abstraction is strongest over static descriptions. Unrestricted closures must not hide live `Q<T>` ownership; see #89.

### 6. Semantic refinement remains explicit evidence

A future/static operation model may carry checked meaning/refinement information, conceptually:

```text
U : Op<A, M>
```

where `M` is evidence-backed semantic information, not an unchecked annotation.

The exact `Meaning` representation is tracked separately. The fixed law is that semantic claims do not arise from names, syntax sugar or optimizer recognition alone.

## Equality/coherence boundary

0.3.0 fixes the distinction:

1. **definitional equality**;
2. **canonical coherence**;
3. **physical map**.

It does **not** require 0.3.0 to choose every concrete implicit coherence rule.

In particular:

- leaf/axis permutation is never ordinary coherence;
- physical maps remain semantically visible;
- any future canonical implicit map must be unique, phase-correct and ownership-preserving;
- the exact 0.4.0 policy for tuple reassociation, unitors, owner pack/unpack and `Bits<0>` lives in #197.

This replaces the older assumption that 0.3.0 itself must finish all surface strictification.

## Ordinary finite functions and staging

The adopted model uses one ordinary finite type universe rather than separate “basis” and “classical” copies.

A function over ordinary finite values may, subject to its typing obligations, eventually be reusable in:

- ordinary runtime classical computation;
- static/compile-time computation;
- checked coherent lifting.

0.3.0 fixes the semantic prohibition:

> **No staging or lifting rule may turn live `Q<T>` into ordinary `T` or hide observation.**

The detailed staging/reuse policy is a 0.4.0 boundary question under #197/#61.

## Preparation and observation

Conceptually, preparation and observation cross the `T / Q<T>` boundary explicitly:

```text
prepare : T -> Q<T>      // effectful according to the adopted preparation class
measure : Q<T> -> T      // only through explicit Observe semantics where supported
```

There is no implicit coercion in either direction.

For `T = Unit`, #43 specifies the special one-dimensional structural facts without creating a general `Q<T> -> T` coercion.

## Product structure

The core laws distinguish:

- type/product structure;
- quantum owner packaging;
- physical axis order.

0.3.0 fixes that:

- axis order remains semantically meaningful;
- ownership never implies separability;
- canonical bookkeeping must not duplicate/drop owners;
- arbitrary isomorphism is not definitional equality.

Which canonical product/unit structure becomes implicit at the surface is deferred to #197.

## Non-goals

0.3.0 does not need to finish:

- every tuple/unit coherence convenience;
- `Bits<0>` normalization;
- all `qfor` carry ergonomics;
- all `qmatch` pattern forms;
- all staging inference;
- all owner pack/unpack sugar.

Those are boundary-specification work for 0.4.0.

It also does not:

- add unchecked casts;
- permit implicit observation/discard;
- make live quantum operations runtime-first-class by default;
- weaken exact phase;
- weaken ancilla cleanup;
- enlarge the trusted verifier merely for surface convenience.

## 0.3.0 acceptance criteria

- [ ] The Reference states `T` vs `Q<T>` as the primary type boundary.
- [ ] `CBit`, `CBits<n>`, and a general source-level `C<T>` are absent.
- [ ] `Γ ; Δ` separates ordinary/static values from linear quantum ownership.
- [ ] Ownership and semantic effects remain orthogonal.
- [ ] #196's `q*** / Q<T> / unmarked` surface rule is consistent with the type system.
- [ ] `Unit / Q<Unit>` follows the same generic law without erasing scalar phase.
- [ ] Static/program descriptions remain distinct from live owners.
- [ ] Definitional equality, canonical coherence and physical maps are distinct categories.
- [ ] No implicit rule chooses between distinct quantum meanings.
- [ ] No implicit conversion reads, discards, duplicates or physically permutes live quantum data.
- [ ] Concrete boundary conveniences are explicitly deferred to #197.

## Compact formulation

> **Ordinary values form the baseline language. `Q<T>` adds linear quantum ownership. `q***` appears only when the construct itself becomes quantum.**

And:

> **0.3.0 freezes the laws; 0.4.0 chooses the canonical conveniences.**

## 2026-10-04 target type contract

Use the shared exact type tree, explicit static context, ordinary context and linear owner context described by the target Reference. Keep ownership separate from effects. Ordinary tuples containing Q fields retain those fields' linear obligations. Common parsing is only the first step; common resolution, generic checking, ownership/effects and lowerings remain implementation work.

The [target Language Reference](https://github.com/MGYamada/Qleisli/blob/codex/v0.3.0-foundation/docs/src/reference/type-model.md) and [foundation analysis](https://github.com/MGYamada/Qleisli/blob/codex/v0.3.0-foundation/docs/src/design/type-foundation.md) record this ordinary implementation decision under the approved 0.3.0 plan and adopted authority hierarchy. Edition remains 2026. This is not a new Guardian interpretation or guarantee admission.

Status: target rules selected; implementation and conformance remain in progress in #307. Current alpha syntax still contains CBit/CBits and general Basis polymorphism is not yet implemented. Required positive and negative tests, exact lowering/interface preservation and native acceptance evidence remain open. Documentation alone does not complete this issue.

## Next implementation unit: shared internal type identity

After the common parser/AST unit, replace the three existing finite, symbolic-sized and concrete-sized type representations with a shared exact tree and shared structural equality/linear classification. Ordinary Bit/Bits leaves and explicit Q ownership are distinct; Unit, Bits<0>, Bit, Bits<1>, immediate tuple arity/nesting and Q<Tuple> versus tuple-of-Q remain different. Existing symbolic Nat equality delegates only to the current checked constraint solver. Q<Unit> is linear regardless of physical width.

This is an internal convergence step, not a new source acceptance rule. Keep current finite/sized profile restrictions and explicit failing lowerer mappings; do not silently add sized Unit owners, finite Bits lowering, general Basis polymorphism or a second implementation of canonical literals. Existing SourceType accessors, CLI shape diagnostics and owner/axis order must retain their current meanings. The next surface cutover will implement ordinary Bit/Bits and 0/1 on the shared checking path, migrate active CBit/CBits sources, and retain historical evidence.

Retain the 22 bounded desired/counterexample inputs and observed diagnostics from the preliminary study, then compare old/new accepted and rejected programs and small native proposals. Both existing checkers must actually use the common structural operations; an unused helper type is not completion. Review finite/semantic evidence mapping and sized provider/preservation/lowering callers independently. This unit neither closes #22/#27/#43/#44 nor proves source preservation or admits a constitutional guarantee.

## Shared type identity implemented — 6daea68

[The implementation](https://github.com/MGYamada/Qleisli/commit/6daea68fe7efb75df0b627f2d20bd7b409f0cfd3) replaces finite, symbolic-sized and concrete-sized type trees with the same Type<N>, exact structural comparison and explicit Q ownership classification. Finite basis/runtime stage and current source-profile restrictions remain explicit. Unit, Bits<0>, Bit, Bits<1>, immediate tuple shape and Q-versus-tuple-of-Q are preserved. The public SourceType accessors retain their old meanings; its derived Rust Debug output intentionally exposes the new private representation and is documented as an observation change.

[Retained packet](https://github.com/MGYamada/Qleisli/blob/6daea68fe7efb75df0b627f2d20bd7b409f0cfd3/tests/fixtures/frontend_v030/shared-types/README.md): 203 tests passed, eight existing cases remained ignored in the selected suites, all 69 executables compiled, 34 observed results and eight small proposal byte sequences matched before/after. Independent review re-compared the original outputs. Latest Rust and MSRV 1.85.0 Clippy pass; inventories cover 238 sources/265 constructors/86 public source files. Hosted run 37203327934 is pending.

This completes the internal identity unit only. Common resolved names/generic judgments, canonical ordinary Bit/Bits and 0/1 migration, source owner/effect rules and lowering obligations remain open. No new source acceptance, general Basis polymorphism or constitutional guarantee was added.
title: 0.3.0 type-theory synthesis: `T`, `Q<T>`, ownership, effects, and semantic refinement
